Found the bug: in sqlparse/sql.py Statement.get_type(), the condition `elif token.ttype != T.Keyword.CTE:` is inverted logic. This should be `==` so that the loop searching for the identifier followed by the DML keyword (SELECT, INSERT, etc.) only runs when the first token actually IS the WITH/CTE keyword. With `!=`, real CTE statements (first token ttype == CTE) skip the loop entirely and fall through to 'UNKNOWN', which matches the reported regression (`assert 'UNKNOWN' == 'SELECT'`). Fixing to `==` restores correct behavior for CTE statements while non-CTE tokens (which don't reach here anyway, since DML/DDL is already handled) remain fine.

I'll fix it and verify with a quick test.

message.content:
Found the bug: in sqlparse/sql.py Statement.get_type(), the condition `elif token.ttype != T.Keyword.CTE:` is inverted logic. This should be `==` so that the loop searching for the identifier followed by the DML keyword (SELECT, INSERT, etc.) only runs when the first token actually IS the WITH/CTE keyword. With `!=`, real CTE statements (first token ttype == CTE) skip the loop entirely and fall through to 'UNKNOWN', which matches the reported regression (`assert 'UNKNOWN' == 'SELECT'`). Fixing to `==` restores correct behavior for CTE statements while non-CTE tokens (which don't reach here anyway, since DML/DDL is already handled) remain fine.

I'll fix it and verify with a quick test.

Found the bug: in sqlparse/sql.py Statement.get_type(), the condition `elif token.ttype != T.Keyword.CTE:` is inverted logic. This should be `==` so that the loop searching for the identifier followed by the DML keyword (SELECT, INSERT, etc.) only runs when the first token actually IS the WITH/CTE keyword. With `!=`, real CTE statements (first token ttype == CTE) skip the loop entirely and fall through to 'UNKNOWN', which matches the reported regression (`assert 'UNKNOWN' == 'SELECT'`). Fixing to `==` restores correct behavior for CTE statements while non-CTE tokens (which don't reach here anyway, since DML/DDL is already handled) remain fine.
